Subject: Unusual request spike from our production tenant — immediate help requested

Hi Stephanie / Redwood team,

We observed a sudden spike of 403 / token-error responses from our integration with Redwood between 2026-10-04 01:05 - 01:18 UTC. Traffic appears to come from a small set of IPs; impact was a transient increase in failed user-facing requests (approx 2.3% of requests over that window). No data exfiltration signs in our logs, but we are escalating internally.

Can you confirm whether there was any service-side change, rollout, or automated token refresh attempt on your end during that window? We also need a point of contact for IR coordination and a copy of Redwood's incident response plan summary and any SOC2/SIG evidence we can reference for our auditors.

Attaching a small pcap snippet and a screenshot of the failing requests from our dashboard.

Attachments: pcap-snippet.txt; request-ack-screenshot.png

Next steps we propose:
- Quick call if you recommend; otherwise a short triage note (what you see/any immediate mitigation).
- Confirm whether any privileged keys were rotated or any service deployments occurred.

Thanks — we need to present initial findings to our security team within 2 hours.

Alex Rivera
Head of Integrations, ClearWave Health

Hi Alex — thanks for the signal and the attachments. Im Neha (Security Ops). High-level summary from our initial internal check:

- No scheduled deploys or key rotations affecting ClearWave between 2026-10-04T01:00-01:30Z.
- Our ingress telemetry shows a short-lived client-side retry loop pattern originating from a small IP range consistent with what you shared.
- No privileged token misuse detected in the first-pass audit. We are continuing deeper log correlation and will check our WAF and rate-limiter logs.

Action items were starting now:
1) Opening an incident record (IR-2026-10-04-CLW) and inviting both teams.
2) Collecting server-side request traces, WAF logs, and GCLB / load-balancer logs for the 00:50-01:50Z window.
3) Requesting a short packet capture (if you have more) and any sequence IDs / example request IDs.
4) We will share a one-page IR summary and the relevant sections of our IR playbook for your auditors.

Can you confirm a preferred mode for sharing logs (we prefer a password-protected share or a secure upload link)? We can also sign an NDA / DPA if needed before we share deeper telemetry. Ive attached a short internal IR summary template and the playbook excerpt that is safe for external sharing.

Attachments: redwood_irp_summary.pdf

- Neha Kapoor

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@clearwavehealth.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example, monica_patel@redwood.example
Date: 2026-10-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Incident close: short-lived client retry loop — postmortem and next steps

Jordan / Alex — following our analysis and the artifacts you provided, were closing IR-2026-10-04-CLW as a security incident with low severity. Key findings: 

- Root cause: a combination of client-side retry storm in ClearWaves SDK (duplicate retries after transient upstream timeouts) and a short-lived rate-limiter misconfiguration at a shared edge layer.
- Impact: 2.3% transient increase in 403-style errors for ~13 minutes; no data access or privileged token exposure detected.
- Fixes applied: Redwood adjusted the edge rate-limiter policy and added a temporary client-specific soft-queue to smooth retries; ClearWave pushed an SDK fix to de-duplicate retry logic.

Were attaching a short postmortem and the IR timeline. As requested, were also sharing our IR playbook excerpt and the SOC2 controls mapping sections applicable to logging and incident response.

Attachments: redwood_irp_summary.pdf; postmortem-IR-2026-10-04-CLW.pdf

Next steps / ask:
- We will publish a joint, sanitized postmortem for your compliance team no later than 2026-10-08.
- Let us know if you need a signed attestation for your auditors mapping the artifacts we shared to your SOC2 evidence request.

Thanks for the quick collaboration.

Ben Carter
Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
